summary: Shodo Fujita is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami and Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a guest researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 1995–2013).

Shodo Harada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Shofukuji under Mumon Yamada (~1962–1982), whom he succeeded. He became abbot of Sōgen-ji in 1982 and founded Tahoma Sogenji Zen Monastery in 1995.

Shogo Watanabe, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Toyo University. His career includes positions at Toyo University, attested in 1991 and serving as professor from approximately 2001 to 2019.

Shohaku Okumura specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Komazawa University and under Kosho Uchiyama. He founded Pioneer Valley Zendo and Sanshin Zen Community, and directed the Soto Zen Buddhism International Center and Soto Zen North America Office (1997–2010).

Shoji Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi. He was a researcher at the Okura Institute (~1971–1976) and an assistant professor (~1976–1985) and professor (~1985–2008) at Toyo University.
Shoju Inaba was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Otani University from approximately 1955 to 1985 and was a part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.
Shojun Bando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1959). He held academic posts at Otani University and Ueno Gakuen University (~1968–1999).

Shokin Furuta specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Matsue High School, Shimane University, the University of Tokyo under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, and Tokyo University of Education, he held professorships at Hokkaido University (~1956–1970) and Nihon University (~1970–1982).
Shoko Kanaoka was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Toyo University, including serving as a professor (attested in 1987 and 2000).

Shoko Miyabayashi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Taisho University (1948–1955), where he later served as lecturer (1960), assistant professor (1962), and Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (1978–2002).
Shoko Takeuchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He later held posts there, including as professor emeritus (attested 1987–1995 and 2009).

Shoko Watanabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Ernst Leumann. He was a professor at Taisho University (1935–1943) and Toyo University (1956–1969).

Shoku Bando is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg (1984–1986), later holding appointments at Kyoto University, Fukui Prefectural College, and Abhidharma Institute in 1987.

Shoren Ihara is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. He held academic posts at Kyushu University, including assistant professor (attested 1959–1965 and 1977), and was a member of the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998).

Shoryu Katsura specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Kyoto University and the University of Toronto under Anthony Kennedy Warder. He was a professor at Hiroshima University (1976–2004) and a director at Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

Shoshin Fukihara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University, Hōryū-ji, and under Join Saeki and Susumu Yamaguchi. His teaching career included posts at Doho University, Shinshu College, Otani Senshu Gakuin, and Otani University Junior College.

Shoshin Ichishima was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served at Taisho University as Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and Professor Emeritus (attested 2014), and worked as a visiting lecturer in Tibetan Buddhism at the University of Hawaiʻi.

Shoshin Kuwayama is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1957–1965) and served there as assistant professor (~1977–1988) and professor emeritus at the Institute for Research in the Humanities.

Shoson Miyamoto was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Otani University, the University of Tokyo, and the University of Oxford. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo, Toyo University, Waseda University, and Komazawa University.
Shou-chien Shih is a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology. He served as a professor at National Taiwan University (~1990–2007) and was director of the National Palace Museum (~2004–2006).
